amendments.body: Fix save compatibility before shipping this. crates/tank_core/src/types/state.rs:174-229 switches canonical concentration reads to net water volume, but crates/tank_core/src/save.rs:8-47 still accepts schema_version 2 saves with no migration. Existing schema-2 saves written under the old gross-volume basis will now load with inflated mg/L and dGH/dKH values and smaller effective water-change/turnover volumes. Either bump the schema and reject old saves or migrate loaded water totals onto the new net-volume basis.
amendments.rationale: This is a silent scientific/data-compatibility regression for every previously saved tank that has substrate.

amendments.body: Update or remove the remaining gross-volume WaterState constructors. crates/tank_core/src/types/water.rs:63-70 and 197-199 still seed totals from TankGeometry::water_volume_l() (gross fill volume), while the rest of the refactor reads chemistry through TankState::water_volume_l() in crates/tank_core/src/types/state.rs:174-229. Any caller that uses WaterState::default_for_geometry, WaterState::from_source_profile, or WaterState::default with a substrate-bearing tank will recreate the same concentration mismatch this change set is meant to eliminate.
amendments.rationale: The public API still contains a correctness trap; internal tests already had to route around these constructors, so external callers can silently rebuild inconsistent states.

payload.summary: Reviewed the net-volume/concentration helper refactor, related scenario/save integration, and the updated tests. I found two correctness issues: old saves are silently incompatible with the new volume semantics, and the public WaterState constructors still initialize gross-volume totals that disagree with the new canonical helpers.
